---
title: "H02: Corticosteroids for systemic use"
description: "ATC H02 corticosteroids for systemic use for modelers: baseline is rhythmic and it moves; duration matters separately from intensity; cumulative exposure is a poor fix."
date: "2026-02-08"
---

**Baseline is rhythmic and it moves.**
Cortisol has a pronounced diurnal pattern, so a constant baseline cannot describe a 24-hour profile [@chakraborty1999]; a time-varying production rate is the usual remedy [@ayyar2019].
Baseline also falls during treatment and recovers slowly after withdrawal [@baker2021; @krzyzanski2021], which is one reason long courses are tapered [@burmester2020].

**Duration matters separately from intensity.**
Fracture risk tracks current daily dose, and adrenal suppression rises with dose *and* treatment duration [@broersen2015adrenal; @magee2002prednisolonepkpd].
An analysis carrying only average concentration misses the duration-dependent toxicities.

**Cumulative exposure is a poor fix.**
A single cumulative-exposure term is a poor fix: it forces duration and intensity to be interchangeable, and can manufacture an apparent exposure-response even when intensity carries no signal at all.
